title: Bilinear Maps in Fewer AND Gates than Rank: A Polynomial Gap Between Multiplicative and Quadratic-Circuit Complexity over F2
description: For n = 4N, every bilinear map F2n × F2n → F2n is computed by a fixed AND-depth-two frame with 2·12N = 2nlog412 = O(n1.7925) AND gates (XOR free); only the wiring depends on the map. By counting, almost every such map has bilinear rank at least n2/3 and therefore needs at least n2/6 AND gates in any quadratic (level-one) circuit. Hence, for almost all bilinear maps, the ratio between quadratic-circuit complexity and multiplicative complexity is at least n0.2075/12 (non-explicit). To the best of our knowledge this polynomial gap is new; it strengthens the single explicit separation 6 < 7 of the companion note. Proofs are in PROOF.md and the PDF; the base frame is checked by a standalone verifier (verify.py). Research note; not peer-reviewed.
references: Mirwald, R., Schnorr, C.-P. (1992). The multiplicative complexity of quadratic Boolean forms. Theoretical Computer Science 102(2), 307-328. doi:10.1016/0304-3975(92)90235-8
Boyar, J., Find, M. G. (2018). Multiplicative complexity of vector valued Boolean functions. Theoretical Computer Science 720, 36-46. doi:10.1016/j.tcs.2018.02.023
Jukna, S. (2006). Graphs and circuits: some further remarks. Dagstuhl Seminar Proceedings 06111. doi:10.4230/DagSemProc.06111.8
